clue.text: Small characters leave playground equipment with branch

indicators.note: the small letter is told to leave, so it is taken away from the equipment's name

parts.note: a swing is a staple of the playground
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Children quit the swings and head for a tree branch instead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small characters' reads as children but supplies only S, the size abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A wing is a branch of an organisation or building, an extension off the main body.

clue.text: Doctor unwise to inject fluid with infection

indicators.note: the abbreviation is injected into the middle of the rearranged letters
to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters of unwise are rearranged

explanation.surface: A careless physician gives an injection of liquid along with an illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is the anagram signal, not a physician; 'to inject' places the abbreviation near the end of the reworked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Swine flu is a viral illness, an influenza strain that passed from pigs to humans.

clue.text: Woman's garment wants belt

definitions.note: the clue's 's is read as 'is', so the definition is the noun Woman

indicators.note: wants here means lacks, so the belt word is missing from the garment

parts.note: a bandanna is a scarf worn on the head or neck
a band is a belt or strip around something

explanation.surface: A lady's outfit needs a belt to finish it off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants' means lacks, not desires: BANDANNA lacking BAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Anna is a female first name, so a woman in crossword shorthand.

clue.text: Maria's bowled over after church appeal

indicators.note: the rearranged name comes after the church abbreviation
being bowled over is being knocked flat, so the letters of Maria's are tumbled

explanation.surface: Maria was overwhelmed following a church appeal for funds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowled over' scrambles the name with its S; 'appeal' is not a request for money but personal allure.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is personal magnetism, the kind of allure that draws people in.

clue.text: God loves hugging liberals after returning each year

indicators.note: the hugging pair comes after the turned-round abbreviation
returning means the abbreviation for each year is read backwards

parts.note: PA is per annum, Latin for each year

indicators.note: the two zeroes wrap around the liberals as if in an embrace

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O; two loves give two
L is the abbreviation for Liberal; two liberals give two

explanation.surface: A deity cherishes left-leaning folk who come back annually.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis scoring love means nil, written O.
explanation.definitionFit: Apollo is the Greek and Roman deity of the sun, music and prophecy.

clue.text: We eat brown fruit, mostly in front of animals

indicators.note: the shortened fruit goes in front of the rest
mostly means most of the fruit's name, its final letter dropped

parts.note: an orange is a citrus fruit

indicators.note: the pronoun swallows the colour, which ends up inside it

parts.note: us is the object form of we
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: We eat a brown fruit, nearly all of it, in front of the creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the fruit's last letter; 'eat' puts the colour inside the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Orangutans are great apes of Borneo and Sumatra, so they are animals.

clue.text: Black businessman ran scams to cut cash on delivery

indicators.note: the rearranged letters cut into the abbreviation, splitting it

parts.note: COD is the familiar abbreviation for cash on delivery

indicators.note: scams is read as the verb, as in fiddles, so the letters of ran are rearranged

explanation.surface: A businessman of colour ran frauds that undercut payment-on-arrival schemes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scams' rearranges and 'to cut' inserts. 'Black' is a surname, not a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Conrad Black is a Canadian-born press baron jailed for fraud, so the clue's businessman.

clue.text: Messenger, for example, climbing north face of Everest

indicators.note: in a down entry climbing means the letters run upwards, read backwards

parts.note: EG is the abbreviation for exempli gratia, for example

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A messenger climbs the north face of Everest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns EG into GE in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A gene carries hereditary instructions from parent to offspring, so it is a biological carrier of messages.

clue.text: Australian conservationist seen in Mayfair window

indicators.note: the name can be seen inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: An Aussie wildlife champion is spotted in a shop window in posh London.
explanation.walkthrough: Mayfair is an expensive district of central London.
explanation.definitionFit: Steve Irwin was the Australian zookeeper and television wildlife presenter known as the Crocodile Hunter.

clue.text: Eccentric, Beryl? Hope that's exaggeration

indicators.note: something eccentric is off-centre and odd, so the two names are scrambled

explanation.surface: Eccentric Beryl tells Hope that what she said was overdone.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyperbole is deliberate overstatement used for effect.

clue.text: Holding note, regular shot to pieces staring down this?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters hold the abbreviation inside them
shot to pieces means wrecked, so the letters of regular are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: NB, nota bene, is the abbreviation used to mark a note

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter, gun steady, peers along the barrel at a target blown apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot to pieces' gives GUREL, and 'Holding' wraps it round the note abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone facing an armed threat stares down the tube of the weapon, the gun barrel.

clue.text: Just back to pinch right cheek

indicators.note: the reversed word pinches the letter, holding it in its middle
back means the word for just is read in reverse

parts.note: just in the sense of fair or level gives even

explanation.surface: Someone simply turns round to pinch a person's cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns EVEN into NEVE; 'to pinch' puts R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve and cheek are both words for impudent boldness.

clue.text: Female, one wearing dresses on expeditions

indicators.note: the pair of letters wears the dresses, so they sit inside them

parts.note: saris are the draped dresses worn in South Asia
A means one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A woman travelling wears traditional dresses on her trips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' means the two letters go inside the garments, not that the garments are worn by the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Safaris are expeditions, especially overland trips in Africa to see wildlife.

clue.text: Pen extremely legible type

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A pen writes in a type that is very easy to read.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pen' is an enclosure, not a writing tool.
explanation.definitionFit: Style and type both mean a kind or sort, as in a style of house.

clue.text: As part of the army, about to tear ligament

parts.note: RE is Latin-derived for about or concerning

indicators.note: tearing the word pulls its letters apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A soldier in the forces is close to tearing a ligament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to tear' rearranges LIGAMENT into GIMENTAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Regimental describes what belongs to a regiment, a unit of the army.

clue.text: 0 plus (-50) plus 500? On reflection, that's the product of a higher power

definitions.text: the product of a higher power

parts.note: the figure zero looks like the letter O

indicators.note: the minus sign takes the number away from the word

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

indicators.note: reflection reverses the abbreviation like a mirror

parts.note: i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: An arithmetic sum, presented as if computed by something more powerful than us.
explanation.walkthrough: '(-50)' strips L from PLUS, leaving PUS; the second 'plus' only links. 'On reflection' turns IE into EI.
explanation.definitionFit: Opus Dei is Latin for work of God, the creation of a higher power.

clue.text: Offspring is a girl

parts.note: Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A child turns out to be a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue is a formal word for children or descendants.

clue.text: See 28
Member unwrapping Italian ham

indicators.note: unwrapping strips the outer layer, the first and last letters of the ham

parts.note: Parma ham is a cured ham from Italy

explanation.surface: Someone takes the paper off a packet of Italian ham.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm is a limb, a member of the body.

clue.text: Out of this world dance move

definitions.meaning: a walk on the moon, literally off our planet
the backward-gliding step made famous by Michael Jackson

explanation.surface: An unearthly piece of choreography.
explanation.definitionFit: Moonwalk names both an astronaut's lunar stroll and a gliding dance step.

clue.text: Longs for order during main revolution

indicators.note: the order abbreviation comes during the reversed sea word, inside it
a revolution turns something round, so the word for main is reversed

parts.note: the main is a poetic word for the sea
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Someone yearns for order amid a seaborne uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' turns SEA into AES; 'during' puts CH in it. The CH is the Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache for something is to yearn or long for it.

clue.text: Guitarist's fantastic writing harmonies without me

definitions.note: the clue's 's is read as 'is', so the definition is the noun

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the pool of letters is rearranged

parts.note: R stands for writing, one of the three Rs

explanation.surface: A guitarist's wonderful songwriting, harmonies without the author's own voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without me' takes M and E out of R plus HARMONIES before 'fantastic' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: George Harrison was lead guitarist of the Beatles.

clue.text: 'Earth and Mars Rocks' by American scholar

indicators.note: rocks as a verb means shakes, so the planet's letters are shaken up

parts.note: US is short for American, as in US forces

explanation.surface: A book title about planetary geology by an American academic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocks' rearranges MARS into RASM.
explanation.definitionFit: Erasmus was the Dutch Renaissance humanist, a great classical scholar.

clue.text: Insecticide found in illegal drink

indicators.note: the name is found inside the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Pesticide is discovered in a bootleg drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldrin is an organochlorine pesticide used to kill insects, now banned.

clue.text: F-fit?

parts.note: the clue reads as a stammered word for healthy, but F is also the musical marking forte, so both halves share one meaning

explanation.walkthrough: Forte, abbreviated F, is literally strong in Italian; fit, as in healthy and robust, is the same answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Strong means powerful and robust, matching fit, and forte in Italian.

clue.text: Look over moves to suppress mad cow disease

indicators.note: the rearranged letters press down on the disease, holding it inside
moves means the letters of over are moved around

parts.note: BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, mad cow disease

explanation.surface: Officials review measures to stamp out a cattle epidemic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look over' tempts as the definition, but 'over' is the anagram fodder; 'moves' gives ORVE and 'to suppress' holds the disease.
explanation.definitionFit: To observe is to watch or notice, so look at.

clue.text: President upset writer touring Delaware …

indicators.note: the reversed word tours round the state, going around it
in an across clue upset means overturned, so the writing tool is read backwards

parts.note: a nib is the writing point of a pen
DE is the US postal abbreviation for Delaware

explanation.surface: A troubled author travels round a US state with the President.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' gives BIN; 'touring' wraps it round the state. Joe Biden represented Delaware in the Senate.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Biden was the forty-sixth President of the United States.

clue.text: Short boy munches a vegetable

indicators.note: the name munches the letter, taking it inside

parts.note: Ben is a short form of Benjamin

explanation.surface: A little lad eats a vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A bean is an edible pod or seed, a common vegetable.

clue.text: … going back over call about electronic victory by Democrat

indicators.note: the call word goes about the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: to ring is to call on the telephone
E is short for electronic, as in e-mail
a win is a victory
D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: Following on, the President's camp replays a call about an online Democratic win.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links this to the previous clue's President.
explanation.definitionFit: Rewinding a tape means running it back over what has played.

clue.text: Singer-songwriter composing eulogy in Norway

parts.note: N is the international vehicle code for Norway

indicators.note: composing puts the letters together in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A musician writes a tribute while in Scandinavia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the fodder, not a link; 'composing' gives EILYOUNG.
explanation.definitionFit: Neil Young is the Canadian rock singer-songwriter of Harvest and Heart of Gold.

clue.text: Main point of government — it's complex

indicators.note: complex means involved and tangled, so the letters of it's are mixed up

explanation.surface: The central idea of government is that it is complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' rearranges ITS into IST.
explanation.definitionFit: The gist is the essence or central idea of something.

clue.text: Area 51 fact: army uncloaked nine aliens, originally left of the birds in a region

definitions.text: of the birds in a region

parts.note: the digits 5 and 1 written as Roman numerals give V and I

indicators.note: originally points to the origin, the first letter, of each of the words before it

explanation.surface: A conspiracy claim: soldiers exposed nine extraterrestrials at the secret base Area 51.
explanation.walkthrough: 51 is split into 5 and 1, not read as Roman LI. Area 51 is a secret US air base linked to UFO lore.
explanation.definitionFit: Avifauna is the bird life of a district, so avifaunal is the adjective for it.

clue.text: In one hand, old bridge partners get clubs

parts.note: the Roman numeral I means one
R stands for right, as in right hand
North and South are partners at the bridge table

explanation.surface: Holding one hand, a pair of veteran card players receive their golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: In contract bridge the four players are named by compass points, North-South against East-West.
explanation.definitionFit: Irons are golf clubs with metal heads, numbered by loft.
